Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

name.description: Server name from .claude/launch.json.

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

limit.description: Max entries to return (default: 50, max: 200).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

Returns {browserOpen, tabs: [{tabId, origin, isActive}]} plus a line saying whether the pane is currently displayed or hidden (a hidden pane still works, but its page runs as a background page, so timing and performance numbers from it can be off; prefer `read_page` / `get_page_text` over screenshots while it is hidden). browserOpen is false (and tabs empty) until `preview_start` or `navigate` opens the pane, so you don't need to call this before opening it.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.description:
Query the status of a Kling AI generation by generation_id. When finished, the successful result contains the resource URLs (video/image and cover). URLs expire in 24 hours, inform user to download in time. 'AI Generated' top-left watermark inherits user web config (separate from bottom-right Kling logo controlled by url / urlWithoutWatermark in query result). Error handling: relay the exact error message to the user in their language, then act per the matching rule below.
| Error type | Message to show | Remediation guidance |
| Content moderation block | The prompt/input media contains disallowed content | Ask for revised input |
| Insufficient credits | Account inspiration credits are insufficient; please top up | Direct the user to the top-up page: https://kling.ai/h5-app/membership-agent?r=agent_Claude Code |
| Model not supported | The selected model does not support this parameter combination | Suggest a viable model and parameters |
| Task timeout | Generation timed out; please resubmit in a moment | Resubmit only when the user explicitly requests it. Make sure all parameters are kept |
| Service error | Service is temporarily unavailable; please retry later | Resubmit only when the user explicitly requests it. Make sure all parameters are kept |

generationId.description: The generationId returned by a generation tool

taskTraceId.description: RFC 4122 UUID V7 identifier to group consecutive, logically connected operations under one user task intent. The same ID is reused for chained steps completing a single goal, such as generating an image then converting it to video for the same subject. A fresh unique UUID must be assigned once the user switches to an unrelated new task, isolating execution traces across distinct user requests.

tools.name: mcp__kling__text_to_image
tools.description: Generate images from a text prompt with Kling AI. Call who_am_i first to discover the available models and each model's argument specification. Returns a generation_id immediately; poll query_tasks for the image URLs.- If user intent or any parameter is uncertain, ask first. Every job is charged; do not submit trial jobs.- If user uses alias words, map to canonical names and pass canonical only. Do not invent names or value.- On timeout/long hang/failure/unexpected result, keep user informed. Ask user whether to retry or change parameters. Do not auto-resubmit or silently change intent/parameters. Constraint: Subject identifiers (Element references, <<<id>>>) are treated as image‐type inputs. Any generation request that explicitly intends to use an element reference must be routed to the image_to_image tool rather than text_to_image. When element‐related intent is clearly detected, switch to image_to_image silently without prompting the user for confirmation.

model.description: Model to use; must be one of the models listed for this tool in who_am_i's availableModels. Required. When the user has no preference, use that tool's defaultModel from who_am_i if present; otherwise choose the model whose description best fits the user's request.

arguments.description: Generation arguments as name/value pairs, e.g. [{"name": "prompt", "value": "a cat"}]. All values are strings. Required names, defaults and allowed values are declared per model in who_am_i.

inputType.description: Must be the literal "URL". url is an already-uploaded http(s) address. Do not use "image" or "video".

inputs.description: Resource inputs as declared per model in who_am_i; each item is {name, inputType: 'URL', url}. Omit when the chosen model declares no inputs.

rationale.description: Detailed purpose explaining the user's core objective for invoking this tool, including contextual reasoning behind parameter selections. Example: "User uploaded a personal artwork image and requested a short animated clip for personal sharing; resolution set to 4K per explicit user demand for maximum visual clarity".

taskTraceId.description: RFC 4122 UUID V7 identifier to group consecutive, logically connected operations under one user task intent. The same ID is reused for chained steps completing a single goal, such as generating an image then converting it to video for the same subject. A fresh unique UUID must be assigned once the user switches to an unrelated new task, isolating execution traces across distinct user requests.

tools.name: mcp__kling__who_am_i
tools.description: Returns the current Kling user's identity and the available generation tools. For each tool: its default model and available models; for each model: the argument specification (required flags, defaults, allowed values) and required inputs. Call this first to confirm that the connection and authorization work, and to learn how to fill in the model, arguments, and inputs parameters for each tool. Pass the default values unless the user explicitly asks for a specific one. Default values may vary between membership tiers. Subscribe to a membership to enjoy faster generation speed and higher clarity (unlock more allowed values). Subject (Element) binding — image subjects and video subjects are different; always call element_get first. (1) Image subjects (cover + secondary, no resource.video) ARE supported on image_to_image for every model that lists an 'elements' argument, INCLUDING kling-image-o1. Do not tell the user that kling-image-o1 or image_to_image cannot use image subjects. (2) Video subjects (resource.video set) are supported ONLY on image_to_video with kling-video-v3_0_omni or kling-video-v3_0. kling-image-o1 and kling-video-o1 do not support video subjects; they still support image subjects where 'elements' is listed. (3) text_to_image and text_to_video support no subjects at all — never pass 'elements' or <<<id>>> there.

Optional list of generation tools to inspect. Each item: text_to_image, image_to_image, text_to_video, image_to_video, motion_control, or omni_ref_video. Pass the tools you are about to use (one or several). Duplicates are ignored. Omit or pass an empty list only to fetch all six tools.

taskTraceId.description: RFC 4122 UUID V7 identifier to group consecutive, logically connected operations under one user task intent. The same ID is reused for chained steps completing a single goal, such as generating an image then converting it to video for the same subject. A fresh unique UUID must be assigned once the user switches to an unrelated new task, isolating execution traces across distinct user requests.

tools.description: Read what is on screen in the user's Terminal panel (shell tabs beside this conversation, where they run their own commands): recent lines with prompts, the commands they typed, and the output. Use it when they refer to something they ran or saw there ("the command I just ran", "this error", "did it pass?") instead of saying you cannot see it. Runs nothing; treat the text as data, not instructions. To start a command there yourself, use run_in_terminal (see also list_terminal_tabs and stop_terminal_tab).

tools.name: mcp__visualize__read_me
tools.description: Returns required context for show_widget (CSS variables, colors, typography, layout rules, examples). Call before your first show_widget call. Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.text:
Господин Шаген, подумал. Отвечу честно по двум разным вещам, потому что «веб-приложение» может означать обе.

**1. Сам VPN через браузер, без приложения: нет.**
Apple и Android не дают сайту управлять VPN на телефоне. Встроенные в телефон способы (IKEv2 и похожие) в России блокируются. Поэтому приложение на телефоне (OneXray, Karing или Happ) остаётся обязательным. Так работают все VPN-сервисы, включая крупные.

**2. Личный кабинет на сайте вместо Telegram: да, можно.**
Это обычный сайт, который делает то же, что бот: регистрация, оплата, выдача ключа, кнопка «Добавить ключ в OneXray», инструкции. Телефон потом подключается через приложение, как и сейчас. Основа для этого у нас уже есть: сервер подписок уже отдаёт страницы по HTTPS, а база клиентов общая, поэтому бот и сайт будут видеть одних и тех же людей.

**Зачем это нужно:**
- для людей без Telegram или тех, кому бот неудобен;
- сайт можно найти в поиске и дать ссылку в рекламе;
- кабинет можно поставить на экран телефона как иконку, будет похоже на приложение.

**Что для сайта понадобится, чего сейчас нет:**
- **Домен.** Сейчас всё работает по IP-адресу, а сайту нужен адрес вроде nexo-vpn.ru. Стоит около 300–1000 ₽ в год.
- **Отдельное место для сайта.** На сервере в Вене порты 80 и 443 заняты самим VPN, трогать их нельзя. Сайт лучше разместить отдельно: на небольшом сервере или на бесплатном хостинге Cloudflare, а он уже будет обращаться к нашему серверу за ключами.
- **Вход без пароля.** Предлагаю код на почту, плюс кнопка «Войти через Telegram» для тех, кто уже в боте.
- **Оплата картой.** На сайте нет Telegram Stars. Нужен ЮKassa или СБП, а для них требуется ИП или ООО. Это отдельный вопрос, его можно решить позже: первую версию кабинета сделаем с пробным периодом, а оплату добавим, когда будут реквизиты.

**Сроки:** первая рабочая версия кабинета, то есть вход, ключ, кнопки для приложений и инструкции, займёт примерно одну-две недели. Бот при этом продолжает работать как есть.

**Что нужно решить сейчас:** делаем ли такой кабинет на сайте. Если да, то первый шаг — выбрать и купить домен, я подскажу, как.

input.prompt:
You are researching for a small Russian VPN service "Nexo" (owner is non-technical; one AI developer). Context you must take as given:
- Servers run Xray (3x-ui) with VLESS over TLS and VLESS Reality (Vienna + Brazil). Clients are in Russia, mostly iPhone and Android.
- Our subscription server already serves: a base64 list of vless:// links, and an Xray JSON array (full configs with our routing rules: Russian banks/Gosuslugi direct, everything else via proxy).
- Today iPhone users use OneXray (recommended), Karing, or Happ. Owner likes OneXray's stability but wants an app of our own: ONE simple screen (big On/Off button, status, server choice, "support"), branded "Nexo", key arrives via a deep link from our Telegram bot. He finds Karing too complex.
- Owner's Mac has only ~6.6 GB free disk, no Flutter/Xcode toolchain; builds would have to run on GitHub Actions. No Apple developer account yet. GitHub account exists.

Your task: a feasibility study of FORKING OneXray (github.com/YuanDevTeam/OneXray, GPL-3, Flutter + libXray, iOS/macOS/Android/Windows/Linux, App Store id6745748773, by Yuan Dev LLC, site onexray.com) into a stripped, rebranded, one-screen app.
Use `gh api` / `gh repo view` to inspect the repo (read-only), the docs/ folder, .github/workflows, pubspec.yaml, ios/ and android/ directories, lib/pages, lib/service. Also read onexray.com docs. Do NOT contact anyone, do NOT fork, do NOT create anything on GitHub.

Find out and report:
1. Code shape: size (files/LOC), how UI pages are organized vs the core service layer; how hard it is to replace the UI with one screen while keeping the connect/subscription/tunnel services. Point to concrete directories/files.
2. Build: does the repo have GitHub Actions workflows that build Android APK and iOS? What do they require (secrets, signing, macOS runners, libXray binaries prebuilt or built from source, Go version)? Is libXray vendored/prebuilt? Estimated CI minutes/cost for iOS builds on GitHub-hosted macOS runners.
3. iOS specifics: Network Extension target, entitlements, App Groups, memory handling for the 50 MB NE limit — how does OneXray deal with it (search for memory/limit/GOGC/debug.SetMemoryLimit etc.).
4. Deep link / subscription import that we already use: onexray://onexray.com/sub/add?url=...&mode=providerManaged — where it is handled; could a fork keep this so our bot's existing buttons work with a custom scheme (e.g. nexo://)?
5. License & naming: GPL-3 obligations for a rebranded fork sold commercially; any trademark/name restrictions in the repo (LICENSE, README, NOTICE); the known GPL-vs-App-Store tension and how projects handle it (author permission/additional permission). Is there a single copyright holder (Yuan Dev LLC) — i.e. could one permission/commercial license solve it? Any contact channel listed (don't contact).
6. Stability reputation: App Store ratings, GitHub issues count/themes (crashes? reconnects? battery?), release cadence.
7. Your estimate: effort in developer-weeks for (a) Android-only one-screen fork with APK distribution, (b) iOS added; main risks; and whether forking OneXray is better or worse than writing a minimal app from scratch on libXray. Give confidence levels.

Report in Russian, ≤ 900 words, structured with headings, concrete file paths and source URLs. State clearly what you verified vs inferred.

input.description: From-scratch minimal VPN app architecture
input.prompt:
You are a senior mobile/network engineer advising a small Russian VPN service "Nexo" (non-technical owner, one AI developer, builds on GitHub Actions, no Apple dev account yet). Servers: Xray (3x-ui) with VLESS+TLS and VLESS Reality; subscription server serves base64 vless:// list and full Xray JSON configs with routing rules. Goal: an own-branded app with ONE simple screen (big On/Off button, status, server pick, support), key via deep link (nexo://...) from a Telegram bot. iPhone is the priority (Russian App Store), Android second.

Task: design and cost a MINIMAL app written from scratch (not a fork), and surface the hidden pitfalls. Research with WebSearch/WebFetch and `gh api` (read-only) the current state (as of late 2026) of:
1. Core options: libXray (github.com/XTLS/libXray — license, gomobile bindings for iOS .xcframework and Android .aar, API surface, who uses it), Xray-core via gomobile directly, sing-box as library (libbox) and its license clause; which is simplest for VLESS Reality + routing.
2. iOS: NetworkExtension PacketTunnelProvider; tun2socks choices (hev-socks5-tunnel, go tun2socks, sing-tun) and how Xray's TUN inbound / "tun" on iOS works; the 50 MB memory limit of the NE process — concrete mitigations used by Happ/OneXray/Karing/FoXray (GOGC, debug.SetMemoryLimit, disabling stats, DNS caching, Go runtime flags); App Groups to pass config; "Always-on/On-demand"; what Apple requires for VPN apps (Guideline 5.4, entitlement com.apple.developer.networking.networkextension, needs paid developer account; is a company account needed for VPN apps?).
3. Android: VpnService + tun2socks or Xray TUN; battery/Doze; Android 14/15 specifics; APK distribution (signing, R8), RuStore/Google Play notes briefly.
4. Framework: Flutter vs React Native vs native SwiftUI + Kotlin for a one-screen app with a Go core: which minimizes risk and build complexity on GitHub Actions; CI cost (macOS runners ~$0.08/min; estimate minutes for an iOS build), code signing on CI (fastlane match, API keys).
5. Realistic plan: milestones, developer-weeks for Android MVP, iOS MVP, polishing; ongoing maintenance load (Xray updates, iOS releases); typical bugs that make such apps "glitchy" (reconnect after network change, sleep/wake, DNS leaks, killed NE process) and how mature apps solve them.
6. Verdict: from-scratch vs fork of an existing Flutter+libXray app — which gives a stable app sooner for a one-person team.

Report in Russian, ≤ 1000 words, with headings, concrete numbers and source URLs; mark verified vs estimated.

input.description: App distribution and legal risks
input.prompt:
You are researching distribution and legal risk for a small Russian VPN service "Nexo" that is considering publishing its OWN branded VPN client app (iOS + Android) for clients in Russia. Owner is non-technical, Russian-speaking. Today clients use third-party apps (OneXray, Karing, Happ) with a subscription link from a Telegram bot. Do not contact anyone; research only (WebSearch extended mode where facts are recent, WebFetch, official sources).

Find out, as of late 2026, with dates and sources:
1. Apple App Store in Russia: history and current state of VPN app removals at Roskomnadzor's request (2024–2026): how many removed, examples, whether removals target apps that advertise "bypass" vs neutral "proxy utility" apps; which Xray clients remain in the RU store (Karing, OneXray, v2RAGE, Npv Tunnel...) and what they have in common (wording, no built-in servers?). Practical rules for app wording/description to survive review and RKN.
2. Apple developer account: individual vs organization (D-U-N-S), cost, whether VPN apps (NetworkExtension entitlement) require an organization account; can a Russian citizen/company currently open and pay for an Apple developer account (payment restrictions), common workarounds (foreign entity); App Review Guideline 5.4 VPN requirements; TestFlight as distribution (limits: 10,000 testers, 90-day builds, review needed) and whether it's used by VPN services in RU as a workaround.
3. Android: Google Play VPN policy (VpnService declaration), RuStore availability for VPN apps (does RuStore accept VPN/proxy clients? examples), direct APK distribution risks (users' "unknown sources"), Huawei AppGallery.
4. Russian law: 2025–2026 rules on VPN "popularization"/advertising fines, blocking of VPN protocols by TSPU (which protocols are blocked/throttled; status of VLESS Reality), any obligations for a VPN service operator/app publisher (registration in RKN registry, "white lists"), liability risk for the owner of a branded app vs. a bot that just hands out keys to third-party apps. Keep it factual, cite sources (RKN, laws, reputable media).
5. Open-source license vs stores: GPL-3 code on the App Store — the known conflict and how projects (VLC, Karing, OneXray) handle it; what a rebranded GPL fork must publish; whether a closed app can use Xray-core (MPL-2.0) and libXray.
6. Summary: a risk matrix (risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation) for: own iOS app, own Android app, staying on third-party apps + web cabinet.

Report in Russian, ≤ 1000 words, headings, sources with dates. Mark what is confirmed vs uncertain.

input.description: One-screen VPN app UX spec
input.prompt:
You are a product/UX researcher. A small Russian VPN service "Nexo" wants its own client app that non-technical Russian users find effortless: owner's words — stable like OneXray, but not complex like Karing. Flow today: user taps "Add key to <app>" in a Telegram bot → the app opens via deep link and imports a subscription (servers in Vienna and Brazil, Russian banks/Gosuslugi routed directly automatically) → user turns VPN on. Tariffs: 7-day trial, 1/3/12 months, up to 3 devices. Compliance constraint: the app must not use words about "bypassing blocks"; neutral wording ("защищённое соединение", "прокси-утилита").

Task: produce a concrete UX specification for a ONE-screen app, grounded in how the best simple VPN apps do it. Research (WebSearch/WebFetch, App Store/Google Play pages, screenshots descriptions, reviews) the UI patterns of: OneXray, Happ, Karing (incl. its "beginner mode"), AmneziaVPN, v2RAGE, Streisand, plus mainstream consumer apps (NordVPN, Proton VPN, Cloudflare WARP 1.1.1.1 — the gold standard of one-button simplicity). Read Russian-language user reviews/complaints about OneXray, Karing, Happ (App Store RU, 4pda, Habr, Telegram) to list the most common confusions and bugs users hit ("не подключается", "нет кнопки", "правила", "подписка не обновляется").

Deliver in Russian, ≤ 1000 words:
1. Top-10 user confusions/complaints with these apps (with sources).
2. The Nexo one-screen spec: layout (what is on screen, exact Russian copy for every label), states (no key / key added / connecting / connected / error / subscription expired / no internet), the deep-link onboarding flow step by step (what the user sees from the bot tap to "connected", including iOS "Allow VPN configuration" prompt), server choice (auto vs Austria/Brazil), "Помощь" and "Поддержка" entry points, how expiry/renewal is shown without payment inside the app (link back to the bot), update of subscription in background.
3. What to deliberately leave OUT (settings, logs, routing editors) and the one hidden "advanced" escape hatch.
4. Accessibility/compliance notes: wording that passes App Store review and avoids RU "VPN popularization" risk.
Include source URLs; mark what is observed vs your design proposal.

  1. «Ссылка не валидна / буфер пуст / timeout при добавлении подписки» — ключ скопирован не целиком или мешает другой включённый VPN. [набл., https://tainet.online/blog/happ-not-working/]

  4. Не появился системный запрос «Добавить конфигурацию VPN» → «нет кнопки / не включается»; рецепт — удалить и переустановить. [набл., https://vk.ru/@happ_keys-happ-ne-rabotaet-reshenie-vseh-chastyh-oshibok-tls-yadro-xra; https://happ-wiki.help/articles/happ-vpn-not-working-2026/]
  5. «Подключено, но сайты не открываются» — старый VPN-профиль в Настройки → VPN, конфликт с VPN на роутере/вторым приложением. [набл., tainet]
  6. «Русские сайты идут не через VPN — значит, не работает?» — split-routing воспринимается как поломка. [набл., tainet]
  7. Переизбыток настроек: правила, TUN/прокси, Mux, Fragment, Noise — Karing даже с beginner-режимом имеет 19 разделов настроек; раздел Custom вылетает при создании профиля. [набл., https://karing.app/en/app-manual/settings; https://nodemaven.com/ru/blog/how-to-set-up-karing/]
  8. Ошибки ядра (TLS handshake, context deadline exceeded, JSON/EOF) показываются «как есть». [набл., tainet]
  9. Приложение исчезает из RU App Store / подделки с похожим названием (Happ → Happ Lite; Streisand, v2RayTun, Amnezia удалялись; у части пользователей в РФ «ни один GUI-клиент не работал»). [набл., https://www.securitylab.ru/news/574268.php; https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/discussions/4759; https://docs.amnezia.org/ru/documentation/instructions/amnezia-on-ios-in-russia]

[набл., https://screensdesign.com/showcase/1111-faster-internet; https://protonvpn.com/support/protonvpn-ios-vpn-app/]
  
  ## 2. Спецификация одного экрана Nexo [предл.]
  
  Раскладка (сверху вниз):
  - Шапка: логотип «Nexo» · справа иконка «?» («Помощь»).
  - Центр: большая круглая кнопка-тумблер (≈200 pt) с текстом «Включить» / «Выключить».
  - Под кнопкой — строка статуса.
  - Карточка сервера: «Маршрут: Автоматически» → лист: «Автоматически (рекомендуем)», «Австрия», «Бразилия», рядом задержка «● 45 мс». Авто = наименьшая задержка.
  - Карточка подписки: «Доступ до 12 янв 2027 · 2 из 3 устройств». Тап → «Продлить в Telegram», «Обновить ключ», «Удалить ключ».
  - Низ: ссылка «Поддержка» (чат бота с ID устройства и последней ошибкой — по согласию).
  Никаких табов, списков серверов, логов, редакторов.
  
  Состояния (кнопка / строка статуса):
  - Нет ключа: кнопка серая / «Ключа пока нет. Получите его в Telegram-боте» + кнопка «Открыть бот».
  - Ключ добавлен: «Включить» / «Готово к подключению».
  - Подключение: «Подключаем…» / «Проверяем маршрут…» (таймаут 15 с → автоматически другой сервер).
  - Подключено: «Выключить», зелёное кольцо / «Защищённое соединение · Австрия · 00:12:34».
  - Ошибка: «Повторить» / одна фраза: «Не удалось подключиться. Проверьте интернет и попробуйте ещё раз» / «Сервер не ответил — пробуем Бразилию» / «Мешает другой VPN. Выключите его в Настройках → VPN». Мелко: «Код: TLS-7».
  - Подписка истекла: кнопка неактивна / «Срок доступа закончился 12 янв» + «Продлить в Telegram».
  - Нет интернета: неактивна / «Нет подключения к интернету».

В боте кнопка «Добавить ключ в Nexo» → `nexo://add?key=…`; Universal Link `https://app.nexo…/add/…` как fallback: если приложение не установлено — страница с App Store/RuStore/APK, после установки ключ подхватывается через буфер/deferred link. [набл.: Happ и панели используют `happ://add/<url>`, https://github.com/Mistgate/mistgate/wiki/Subscriptions; OneXray — «OneXray Links»]
  2. Лист «Добавить ключ Nexo?» · «Доступ до 7 ноя 2026 · пробный период» · «Добавить» / «Отмена».
  3. Экран-прокладка: «Сейчас iPhone спросит разрешение добавить конфигурацию VPN. Это стандартный запрос системы — нажмите „Разрешить" и подтвердите код-паролем», кнопка «Продолжить». (Так делает Cloudflare перед системным промптом.) [набл., screensdesign]
  4. Системный промпт iOS «Nexo хочет добавить конфигурации VPN» → Allow + Face ID/код. Android: диалог «Запрос на подключение» → OK.
  5. Если «Не разрешать»: состояние «Ключ добавлен» + подсказка «Без разрешения соединение не включится. Нажмите „Включить" и выберите „Разрешить"».
  6. Автовключение → «Подключено». Тост: «Банки и Госуслуги работают напрямую — так и задумано».
  7. Повторный тап по ссылке из бота с уже добавленным ключом → обновляет ключ без дубля.
  
  Обновление подписки в фоне: тихий fetch при каждом запуске и каждом «Включить» (User-Agent `Nexo/1.x`); раз в 6 ч через BackgroundTasks/WorkManager; 401/410 → «Подписка истекла»; 3 неудачи подряд → принудительное обновление ключа и смена сервера. Кнопка «Обновить ключ» остаётся для ручного случая.

  «Помощь»: 5 раскрывающихся пунктов: «Не подключается», «Подключено, но не открывается», «Банки не работают», «Как добавить второе устройство», «Как продлить», каждый с кнопкой «Написать в поддержку».
  
  ## 3. Что сознательно убираем
  - Экран «Настройки», DNS, TUN/прокси-режим, Mux, Fragment, Noise, IPv6, порт, NTP, редактор правил, импорт JSON, логи, тест скорости, список нод, QR-сканер, ручной ввод конфига (ключ только из бота или из буфера, если скопирован `nexo://`).
  - Один скрытый люк [предл.]: долгое нажатие (3 с) на логотип → лист «Диагностика»: «Скопировать отчёт для поддержки» (версия, ОС, последние 50 строк лога ядра, код ошибки) и переключатель «Резервный способ подключения» (альтернативный транспорт/порт). Редактировать нельзя.

  - Кнопка ≥44 pt, VoiceOver «Включить защищённое соединение», статус через accessibility announcement, Dynamic Type, цвет состояния дублируется текстом и иконкой.

Формулировка по образцу OneXray: «клиент для защищённого соединения с вашим сервером». [набл., https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6745748773; https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/]

С бесплатным **Provider ID** (регистрация на happ-proxy.com, ✅ docs/provider-id) открываются «провайдерские» параметры: `hide-settings` (скрыть конфиги от клиента), `sub-expire` + `sub-expire-button-link` (кнопка «Продлить» за 3 дня до окончания), `sub-info-*` (свой инфоблок с кнопкой), `new-url`/`fallback-url` (смена домена подписки без участия клиента), `notification-subs-expire`, `subscription-autoconnect`. Логотип/имя приложения заменить нельзя — только название профиля, цвета и кнопки. Deep link `happ://add/<sub-url>`. White-label-программы у Happ нет (⚠️ не найдено).
  **Статус в RU App Store**: базовый Happ удалён 28.03.2026 по требованию РКН; версия **Happ Lite** (Flyfrog LLC, v5.8.1) вернулась в российский App Store — SecurityLab, 12.09.2026 ✅, с оговоркой «может исчезнуть снова».
  
  **v2RayTun** ⚠️. Поддерживает `profile-title`, `subscription-userinfo`, `announce` (PasarGuard commit: announce «только Happ и v2RayTun»), deep link `v2raytun://import/`. Отдельной программы брендирования для провайдеров не найдено. Удалён из RU App Store 28.03.2026 (Kod.ru, 3DNews), возврата не найдено.
  
  **Streisand** ⚠️. Только импорт подписки (deep link есть по вторичным данным), заголовки брендирования не документированы. Удалён из RU App Store 28.03.2026.
  
  **Karing** ✅ (karing.app/cooperation/connect; /en/cooperation/custom/skiapp). ISP-cooperation = «вход = подписка»: провайдер регистрируется на harry.karing.app (PID), ставит на сайт страницу с `karing.js` и вызывает `_karing.config(PID, nick, subUrl, name)`; в меню Karing закрепляются ваш сайт/FAQ/поддержка/соцсети, рекламный слот «только ваш сервис», push-уведомления о продлении. Кастомный лого/имя — в планах («todo»). Полные примеры только для V2Board/SSPanel (3x-ui/Remnawave не упомянуты). Платный листинг в «рекомендациях» — цена не опубликована. Отдельно есть **custom-клиент**: свой логотип, цвета, имя, Android-package, платежи (IAP/коды/редирект), «3–5 дней» на интеграцию панели — iOS в списке не указан, цена не опубликована, контакт t.me/ovowe. Наличие Karing в RU App Store — ⚠️ не подтверждено.
  
  **OneXray** ⚠️ (onexray.com/docs). Документированы HTTPS-подписки с age-шифрованием и HWID, есть раздел «Remnawave provider configurations» (не открылся). Заголовки `profile-title`/`announce` — по спецификации Xray-core discussion #4877, в доках OneXray прямо не найдены. Клиент «без серверов и подписок»; RU-доступность не подтверждена.
  
  **Hiddify** ✅ (wiki hiddify-app/URL-Scheme): `profile-title` (base64 с эмодзи), `profile-web-page-url`, `support-url`, `profile-update-interval`, `subscription-userinfo`. GPLv3 — можно форкать; white-label-программы нет ⚠️.
  
  **INCY** удалён из RU App Store 27.10.2026 (Kod.ru) ✅ — иллюстрация риска.
  
  # 2. White-label / «своё приложение под ключ»
  
  Специализированных RU-вендоров «брендированный Xray-клиент с публикацией в App Store» в открытых источниках **не найдено** (habr, 4pda, kwork, searchengines — ⚠️ пусто). Найдено:

  - **VPNGN/VPNWholesaler** ⚠️: брендированный вариант от $10 000 предоплаты, «только избранным партнёрам».

  # 3. Промежуточный вариант: брендированная страница подписки / Mini App
  
  - **Remnawave subscription-page** ✅ (remna.st docs): Docker, `app-config.json` с полями name/logoUrl/supportUrl и списком приложений по платформам с `urlScheme` (`happ://add/` и др.), `isFeatured`. Темы: legiz-ru/material-remnawave-subscription-page. Требует панели Remnawave (3x-ui не поддерживается напрямую).
  - **3x-ui** ✅ (docs/custom-subscription-templates.md, PR #5079): свой `index.html` на Go-шаблонах с `{{ .subUrl }}`, `{{ .subTitle }}`, `?format=info` для живого статуса — можно сделать страницу Nexo с кнопками «Добавить в Happ/OneXray/Karing» за 1–2 дня.
  - **Telegram Mini App** ✅: maposia/remnawave-telegram-sub-mini-app (Next.js, CRYPTO_LINK для Happ, REDIRECT_LINK для Windows-deeplink), 3252a8/remnawave-minishop (бот + web app: оплата, триал, инструкции по установке), rez-code/remnashop. Для 3x-ui аналогов нет — адаптация ~1–2 недели.
  - Трюк JustYay/redirect-page: промежуточная страница для deeplink `happ://` из Telegram Desktop.

  ✅ Guideline 5.4: VPN-приложения только через NEVPNManager, **только от организаций**, нельзя нарушать местные законы; при наличии лицензионных требований в стране — указать лицензию в Review Notes; нарушителей удаляют и могут исключить из Developer Program.

Это снижает «видимость», но **не** защищает от запроса РКН — Apple удаляет по требованию регулятора независимо от типа листинга (⚠️ прямого прецедента для unlisted-VPN не найдено). Господин Шаген, ниже отчёт по минимальному собственному приложению Nexo (iOS + Android). Пометки: **[V]** — проверено по первоисточнику (gh api / сайт), **[E]** — оценка.

## 1. Ядро: что брать

| Вариант | Лицензия | Состояние (31.10.2026) | Вывод |
|---|---|---|---|
| **libXray** (XTLS) | MIT [V] | релиз v26.10.29, привязан к Xray-core v26.10.29; API единая `Invoke(json)` с методами `runXray/stopXray/pingBatch/testXray/convertShareLinksToXrayJson/decodeSubscriptionText/getFreePorts`; сборка `python3 build/main.py android|apple gomobile|apple go` → .aar / LibXray.xcframework [V] | **Брать.** Встроенный модуль `memory` для iOS: `SetGCPercent(10)`, `SetMemoryLimit(30 MiB)`, `FreeOSMemory()` раз в секунду [V] |
| Xray-core напрямую через gomobile | MPL-2.0 [V] | официальных мобильных биндингов нет; libXray и есть эта обёртка | Не нужно |
| sing-box / libbox | GPL-3.0 + запрет на использование имени [V] | мощнее (sing-tun внутри), но GPL обязывает открыть исходники клиента | Для закрытого брендированного клиента — риск |

Критичное: Xray-core с января 2026 имеет **TUN-inbound с поддержкой iOS** — fd из NetworkExtension передаётся через `env.xray.tun.fd` (PR #5612, merged 26.01.2026 [V]). Отдельный tun2socks (hev-socks5-tunnel, MIT [V]; go tun2socks) **не обязателен**: в конфиг подписки добавляем inbound `tun`, остальной JSON с routing-правилами с вашего сервера идёт как есть. Ограничение: один Go-runtime на процесс — нельзя линковать libXray вместе с другой Go-библиотекой [V].
Источники: https://github.com/XTLS/libXray , https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/5612 , https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/blob/dev-next/LICENSE

## 2. iOS — главные подводные камни

- **Лимит памяти NE-процесса: 50 MiB** на iOS 15–18 (Apple DTS, сентябрь 2024; про iOS 26 ответа нет; на iOS ≤14 — 15 MiB) [V]. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/73148 . Митигации, реально применяемые: GOGC=10 + `SetMemoryLimit` (libXray: 30 MiB; hiddify/libbox: `SetMemoryLimit(true)`) [V]; отключить `stats`/`api` в конфиге, `loglevel: warning`, не грузить полные geoip/geosite.dat (OneXray кладёт dat-файлы в App Group и подгружает в extension) [V по коду OneXray]; MTU ~1500, ограничить число соединений [E].
- **Guideline 5.4** (дословно): VPN-приложения обязаны использовать NEVPNManager и **«may only be offered by developers enrolled as an organization»**; требуется экран с декларацией данных до покупки/использования; нарушение — удаление и возможное исключение из программы [V]. https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#5.4 . Значит: нужен **Organization-аккаунт ($99/год, D-U-N-S юрлица)**; Individual-аккаунт для VPN отклоняют [V, форумы]. **Из России оплата enrollment в 2026 фактически не проходит** (Mir/Visa/мобильный счёт отклоняются, thread/850823, октябрь 2026 [V]); Enterprise-программа закрыта для РФ с февраля 2025 [V]. # Nexo: своё приложение vs сторонние клиенты — риски (данные на 31.10.2026)

Пометки: **[✓]** — подтверждено источниками; **[?]** — неподтверждено/противоречиво.

## 1. App Store в России

- **Масштаб [✓].** Удаления по запросам РКН: 2022 — 7, 2023 — 12, 2024 — 171, 2025 — 1 213 приложений из RU-витрины (Apple Transparency Report, цит. te-st.org 02.08.2026, securitylab 27.10.2026). GreatFire: к 16.09.2024 недоступны 98 VPN; РКН официально признавал 25.
- **2026 [✓].** 28.03 — удалены Streisand, V2Box, v2RayTun, Happ‑Proxy Utility (всего ~20, по Kod.ru). 24.06 — Happ Plus; 29.06 вернулся как «Happ — Proxy Utility+», снова удалён в августе; 10–12.09 вернулся как Happ Lite (Flyfrog LLC); 27.10 — удалён INCY, **Apple отключила ему и TestFlight в РФ** (все виды ссылок).
- **Механизм [✓].** РКН ссылается на ст. 15.1 149‑ФЗ (информация о способах доступа к запрещённым ресурсам); Apple удаляет **поимённо**, без суда, за несколько дней, письмо «content illegal in Russia». Автоматического поиска по описанию нет: «Happ Plus» с тем же функционалом стоял до тех пор, пока его не назвали (te-st.org).
- **Нейтральные формулировки не спасают [✓].** INCY и Happ Lite писали «не предоставляем серверов, пользователь сам отвечает за закон» — удалены. Пока в RU‑магазине остаются Karing (SUPERNOVA NEBULA LLC), OneXray (Yuan Dev LLC), v2RAGE, XRay Connect [? — проверять еженедельно]. Общее: без встроенных серверов, «proxy utility/client», иностранные юрлица, нет слов «обход блокировок/Россия/YouTube».
- **Практические правила:** описание как «клиент для подключения к вашим серверам по VLESS/Reality/Hysteria2», без «VPN для России», скриншоты без упоминания заблокированных сервисов, Privacy‑декларация до оплаты (Guideline 5.4), сервера раздаются только после входа. Это снижает риск отказа на ревью Apple, но не защищает от именного запроса РКН.

## 2. Аккаунт разработчика Apple

- **Guideline 5.4 [✓]:** VPN‑приложения — только через NEVPNManager API и **только от аккаунтов типа Organization**; нарушение — удаление и возможное исключение из программы. Технически entitlement packet‑tunnel доступен любому платному аккаунту без одобрения (DTS Apple, форум, март 2026), но в сторе индивидуала с VPN не пропустят.
- **Organization [✓]:** нужен D‑U‑N‑S, юрлицо (не ИП/бренд), $99/год. Российские карты и «Мир» не проходят, оплата со счёта телефона закрыта с апреля 2026; рабочий путь — иностранная карта/юрлицо (vc.ru, DTF 2026). Платные приложения от РФ‑аккаунтов ограничены РФ‑аудиторией [?]. Enterprise‑программу россиянам закрыли 12.02.2025 [✓].
- **TestFlight [✓]:** до 10 000 внешних тестеров, 100 внутренних, сборка живёт 90 дней, первая внешняя сборка проходит Beta App Review. Используется в РФ как запасной канал (ProxysVPN, Happ), но кейс INCY показал: Apple отключает TestFlight вместе с приложением.

## 3. Android

- **Google Play [✓]:** политика VpnService — VPN должен быть core‑функцией, декларация в Play Console, видео ≤90 с, раскрытие данных внутри приложения, шифрование, запрет перенаправления трафика ради монетизации. Запросы РКН идут через Таганский суд (Google оштрафован на 22,8 млн ₽, февраль 2026); в марте 2026 — рекордные 233 требования, но большинство приложений остались (iStories 08.04.2026, te-st.org). Канал более устойчив, но не гарантирован.
- **RuStore [?]:** официальных правил по VPN нет; с 2023 г. РКН готовил критерий «не даёт доступ к реестру запрещённых»; в апреле 2026 RuStore анонсировал свой VPN без YouTube/Telegram за 999 ₽/мес. Xray‑клиентов (Happ, v2rayNG, Hiddify) в каталоге не найдено. Публикация Nexo там нереалистична.
- **Прямой APK [✓]:** работает, но нужны reproducible builds, опубликованный отпечаток подписи и обновления своими силами; в мае 2026 фиксировали «бесплатный VPN» с банковским трояном — пользователи боятся «неизвестных источников». С мая 2026 Ozon/WB/2ГИС/RuStore собирают список VPN‑клиентов на телефоне (iXBT 02.05.2026).
- **AppGallery [?]:** сообщений об удалениях нет; статус неизвестен.

## 4. Российское право

- **Реклама/популяризация [✓]:** 281‑ФЗ/282‑ФЗ от 31.07.2025, с 01.09.2025: ч. 18 ст. 14.3 КоАП — граждане 50–80 тыс. ₽, должностные 80–150 тыс., юрлица 200–500 тыс.; повторно для юрлиц до 1 млн (РБК 22.05.2026). К началу 2026 сумма штрафов >19 млн ₽. Запрет распространения информации о способах обхода (с 01.03.2024, расширен 30.11.2024 на научно‑техническую) — основание для блокировок сайтов/ботов.
- **Обязанности оператора VPN [✓]:** по ст. 15.8 149‑ФЗ владелец после предписания РКН обязан подключиться к ФГИС и фильтровать реестр; отказ — блокировка; к концу февраля 2026 заблокировано 469 сервисов (439 к январю). Реестра «легальных VPN» нет. Штрафы за неподключение существуют (цифра «до 8 млн» — [?], не подтверждена первоисточником).
- **Проект Минцифры 01.10.2026 [✓ как проект]:** реестр владельцев VPN‑обхода + запрет российского хостинга на 1 год. Не принят.
- **ТСПУ [✓/?]:** с декабря 2025 блокируются SOCKS5, VLESS, L2TP; 17.02.2026 — массовая блокировка VLESS+Reality+TCP у проводных операторов; с мая–июня 2026 — поведенческая «заморозка» по ASN+JA3+залпам хендшейков (Habr 15.06.2026, реконструкция, не официально); с августа — блокировки подсетей хостеров (te-st.org 30.09.2026). Относительно живы: gRPC/XHTTP‑Reality, Hysteria2, SSH [?].
- **Бренд‑приложение vs бот [оценка]:** закон не различает их; привлекают за **рекламу/популяризацию** и за **неисполнение предписания**. Своё приложение в сторе с юрлицом‑издателем и платёжными данными — это идентифицируемый «владелец сервиса»; бот + сторонние клиенты оставляют ту же ответственность, но меньше публичных следов. Уголовных дел против продавцов подписок в открытых источниках не найдено [✓ на дату].

## 5. Лицензии

- **GPL vs App Store [✓]:** VLC снят в январе 2011 из‑за несовместимости условий App Store (DRM/usage rules) с GPLv2; вернулся в 2013 после релицензирования (LGPL/MPL). Проблема актуальна для GPLv3 так же.
- **Karing [✓]:** GPL‑3.0+ с запретом использовать имя/намекать на связь — форк обязан публиковать исходники и не может быть закрытым.
- **OneXray [✓]:** GPL‑3.0 + «VPN Provider Exception»: провайдер VPN вправе собирать **закрытый ребренд для своего сервиса**, не раскрывая код (условия в файле LICENSE‑EXCEPTION — проверить). Для Nexo это самый чистый путь.
- **Xray‑core — MPL‑2.0, libXray — MIT [✓]:** закрытое приложение может их использовать; при модификации файлов Xray‑core нужно публиковать изменённые файлы.

## 6. Матрица рисков

| Android: прямой APK — недоверие/подделки | Средняя | Средний | Reproducible builds, страница проверки подписи |

**Вывод:** собственное iOS‑приложение даёт бренд, но в 2026 г. живёт в RU App Store месяцами и требует иностранного юрлица; Android‑приложение (Play + APK) умеренно реалистично; минимальный правовой и операционный риск — сторонние клиенты + веб‑кабинет, при желании — закрытый ребренд OneXray для Android как первый шаг.

- **UX-спецификация одного экрана** получена (кнопка Включить/Выключить, статус, маршрут Авто/Австрия/Бразилия, карточка подписки, «Поддержка», состояния ошибок простыми фразами, продление через бот).

Господин Шаген, все шесть отчётов пришли, я их сверил между собой и перепроверил ключевые факты сам. Вот итог.

## Главный вывод

**Лучший путь: своё приложение Nexo на основе OneXray.** Именно сегодня, 31 октября, авторы OneXray добавили официальное разрешение: VPN-сервис может взять их код и сделать закрытое приложение под своим брендом, ничего не публикуя. Я проверил это в их репозитории сам. Это снимает главную юридическую проблему, которая была с Karing.

**Почему OneXray, а не другие:**
- Его код устроен так, что экраны и «движок» разделены. Можно выкинуть все сложные экраны и оставить один наш, а движок, тот самый стабильный, остаётся.
- Готова сборка на GitHub: Android собирается за 15 минут, бесплатно.
- Кнопка «Добавить ключ» из бота уже работает с ним, достаточно поменять название ссылки на `nexo://`.
- **Karing отпал окончательно:** часть его кода закрыта, из открытого кода его собрать нельзя. Hiddify запрещает коммерческое использование.
- Готовые «арендованные» приложения под чужой бренд: достойных вендоров нет, а один западный просит около 90 тысяч рублей в месяц. Не стоит.

## Как будет выглядеть приложение

Один экран: большая кнопка «Включить / Выключить», строка статуса, выбор маршрута «Автоматически / Австрия / Бразилия», срок доступа с кнопкой «Продлить в Telegram», внизу «Поддержка». Ошибки показываются простыми фразами, например «Мешает другой VPN. Выключите его в настройках». Никаких настроек, логов и правил. Полная спецификация экрана уже готова.

## Порядок работы

**Этап 1. Android, примерно 3–4 недели.** Раздача через кнопку в боте (файл APK), потом Google Play (25 долларов разово). Затрат на сборку нет.

**Этап 2. iPhone, позже.** Здесь два серьёзных препятствия, и они не технические:
1. Apple разрешает VPN-приложения только от аккаунта **организации**: нужно юрлицо, регистрация D-U-N-S, 99 долларов в год. Оплата из России в 2026 году практически не проходит, то есть нужно **иностранное юрлицо**.
2. В 2026 году Роскомнадзор добился удаления из российского App Store почти всех таких приложений, включая Happ, v2RayTun, Streisand, а 27 октября INCY вместе с TestFlight. Наше приложение станет такой же мишенью. Поэтому даже со своим приложением OneXray и Karing останутся в боте как запас.

Пока iPhone остаётся на OneXray через бот, как сейчас.

## Что важно по закону

<built_in_browser>
You have a built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser or the browser pane: a real browser with tabs inside the Claude desktop app, isolated from the user's Chrome, with its tools already loaded. You can use it for web research, reading pages and docs, checking staging or a deployed app, filling forms, and previewing this project's dev servers. `preview_start` with a `url` opens a site in its own tab; prefer `get_page_text` / `read_page` over screenshots for reading. The user sees the same pane and can take over; they may be asked to allow a site first, and if a site is refused or declined, tell them and move on rather than retrying. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<simulator_tools>
When the user wants to run, test, or visually check an iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?"), use mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control. Simulators and emulators only — when the user asks to run on their physical device ("on my phone", "on my device"), build for the device with your normal build tools instead; these tools and the panel cannot drive a real device. Open the live panel ('attach') whenever the user would want to see the app themselves — and call 'attach' FIRST, before you build or launch: it is cheap, it opens instantly on a booted device (and surfaces the one-time device-access prompt while the user is still at the keyboard), and if nothing is booted it returns a harmless, clear error — boot or build first in that case, then attach as soon as a device is up. Do not defer the panel to the implicit re-attach in 'launch'; the panel should already be open while you build. The panel is the user's view; your own verification (screenshot, tap, text) is headless and works without it — verify yourself rather than asking the user to check. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. If 'attach' fails, follow the error's remediation: address the cause (for example no booted device, or device access not granted) or tell the user — don't retry the same call in a loop unless the error says retrying will work. If the failure is the host's Xcode setup (a wrong xcode-select, missing Xcode, or a missing iOS platform), tell the user right away with the exact fix the error gives — most of these fixes need their password, so you cannot run them (the error itself says when a fix is one you can run) — and if you continue by driving the Simulator app with generic screen tools instead, say so explicitly; never switch silently. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.
</simulator_tools>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste.
